mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential housing starts and consumer spending (as measured by RSAFS) indicate weakening aggregate demand, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing supply shock regime (indicated by a 3-month decline in industrial production), negative S&P 500 returns occur over the next 20 trading days due to inflationary pressures and reduced corporate output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances during the manufacturing supply shock regime.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 1.5% year-over-year indicates strengthening economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of quarters where GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI inflation rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals accelerating inflation, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to anticipated central bank rate hikes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a labor market contraction, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity slows.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both decline > 0.3% from prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both PAYEMS and UNRATE decline > 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic regime (indicated by GDP growth above 2.5% and unemployment below 4.0%), a decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST < 1300 during late-cycle expansion.
